title: Introduce Econ Architect: tenant-level defaultifier for batching/caching and quant profiles
author: Priya Raman
description:
Context and motivation: Tenant onboarding often requires hand-tuned batching, cache defaults, and quantization profiles to hit unit-econ targets. This PR introduces the 'Econ Architect' pipeline: a declarative synthesizer that proposes tenant-level default policies (batch shapes, cache TTLs, KV-prefill heuristics, and recommended quant profiles) based on a sampled workload signature and historical latency/cost telemetry. Motivation: reduce manual ops for customers, provide safe, reversible defaults that improve P95 latency and token unit cost for typical conversational and embed-heavy tenants.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new service package redwood/econ_architect that analyzes a tenant's workload sample and telemetry to synthesize a set of defaults.
- Extends tenant defaults schema (api/v1/tenant_defaults.proto) with opt-in fields: batching_profile_hint, cache_policy_hint, quant_profile_recommendation, and safe_rollout_policy.
- Introduces a CLI command `redwood econ-architect compile --tenant <id> --sample=<s3://...>` which runs the synthesizer in dry-run and export modes.
- Runtime integration: a non-invasive stage in the defaults-apply pipeline that can produce a preview bundle and optionally apply safe rollouts to Dedicated pools (bounded throughput, canary ramp).
- Telemetry: small telemetry bridge for the synthesizer to emit scoring metrics (expected_unit_econ_delta, risk_score, rollback_probability).
- Tests: unit tests for algorithm heuristics and an integration test that runs the CLI against a recorded sample and validates no regressions on latency SLOs in synthetic runner.

Checklist: 
- [x] Schema change + migration path and backward compatibility preserved (fields are optional).
- [x] Unit tests for core heuristics (batch/caching/quant scoring).
- [x] Integration test for CLI dry-run and apply against a small local Dedicated dev cluster.
- [x] Telemetry hooks instrumented and privacy-reviewed.
- [x] Docs + examples in docs/tenant_defaults/econ-architect.md

Risk and safety: The synthesizer only suggests defaults; apply path requires `force-apply` and an explicit safe_rollout_policy. The runtime apply stage has safeguards: rate limits to avoid wide blasts, a canary lane capped at 5% of traffic, and an automatic rollback trigger if P95 latency increases > 15% or error rates spike. The change avoids any automatic cross-tenant config mutations; every change is namespaced per-tenant and logged for audit.

Related work: ENG-2210 (tenant defaults automation), design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2210/econ-architect-design, earlier prototype in pr-312468 was an experimental sampler; this PR implements a production-ready path with safety controls.

Commit summary: 3 commits
- feat(econ_architect): initial synthesizer + scoring pipeline (core algorithm + model signatures)
- feat(cli): add `redwood econ-architect` command and dry-run/export handlers
- test/telemetry/docs: unit/integration tests, telemetry bridge, and docs for operator flow

Changed areas (high level files):
- api/v1/tenant_defaults.proto (schema additions)
- services/econ_architect/* (new package: analyzer, scorer, rollout_safety)
- cmd/redwood/commands/econ_architect.go (CLI entrypoint)
- runtime/defaults_applier.go (hook to produce preview bundles and safe apply)
- integration/tests/econ_architect_integration_test.go
- docs/tenant_defaults/econ-architect.md

Release notes: Adds `Econ Architect` opt-in synthesizer for tenant default recommendations (batching, cache, quant). Disabled by default; operators can enable and audit suggestions. Provides CLI for dry-run and export.

How to validate locally: follow docs/tenant_defaults/econ-architect.md to run `make dev-cluster` then `redwood econ-architect compile --tenant test-tenant --sample ./testdata/sample.json --dry-run` and inspect the preview bundle in /tmp/econ-preview.json.

Observability dashboards for the scoring metrics live at observability/dashboards/econ-architect.json.
